blocks.explanation: Yeh "show that" yani proof ka sawal hai: humein koi number nahin nikaalna, balke dikhana hai ke left side aur right side barabar hain. \(\operatorname{Re}(z)\) ka matlab \(z\) ka real part hai: \(z = a + ib\) ho to \(\operatorname{Re}(z) = a\). Plan: left side mein \(z\) aur \(\overline{z}\) ki values daalenge, simplify karenge, aur dekhenge ke aakhir mein sirf \(a\) bachta hai. Is result ka faida: \(z\) aur us ka conjugate jama karne se imaginary hissa cancel ho jata hai.
steps:
Step 1: \(z = a + ib\) farz karein
\[z = a + ib\]
\[\overline{z} = a - ib\]
Kyun: Yeh general complex number hai, jo har \(z \in C\) ko represent karta hai. Conjugate mein sirf \(ib\) ka sign badalta hai.

Step 2: \(z\) aur \(\overline{z}\) ko add karein
\[z + \overline{z} = (a + ib) + (a - ib)\]
\[= 2a\]
Kyun: Real parts jama hue: \(a + a = 2a\). Imaginary parts \(+ib\) aur \(-ib\) aapas mein cancel ho gaye. Yahi is sawal ka asal nukta hai.

Step 3: 2 se divide karein
\[\dfrac{z + \overline{z}}{2} = \dfrac{2a}{2} = a\]
\[= \operatorname{Re}(z)\]
Kyun: \(2a/2 = a\), aur \(a\) hi \(z\) ka real part hai. Left side right side ke barabar ho gayi.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal \(z = 3 + 4i\): \((3 + 4i + 3 - 4i)/2 = 6/2 = 3\), aur \(3 + 4i\) ka real part waqai 3 hai. Khud sochiye: \(z = -2 + 7i\) ke liye kya aayega?
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\dfrac{z + \overline{z}}{2} = \operatorname{Re}(z)\) (number aur us ke conjugate ka average sirf real part deta hai).

blocks.explanation: Yeh bhi proof hai, part (i) ka jora. \(\operatorname{Im}(z)\) imaginary part hai, yani \(z = a + ib\) mein woh real number \(b\) jo \(i\) ke saath laga hai (\(i\) ke baghair). Pichle part mein jama karne se \(ib\) cancel hua tha; is baar minus karenge to ulta \(a\) cancel hoga aur \(ib\) bachega. Plan: \(z\) mein se \(\overline{z}\) minus karein, phir \(2i\) se divide karke sirf \(b\) tak pohanchein.
steps:
Step 1: \(z = a + ib\) farz karein
\[z = a + ib\]
\[\overline{z} = a - ib\]
Kyun: Complex number aur us ke conjugate ki general shakal; is se proof har \(z\) ke liye sach hoga.

Step 2: \(z\) mein se \(\overline{z}\) minus karein
\[z - \overline{z} = (a + ib) - (a - ib)\]
\[= a + ib - a + ib\]
\[= 2ib\]
Kyun: Bracket se pehle minus ho to andar ke dono signs badal jate hain: \(-(a - ib) = -a + ib\). Phir \(a - a = 0\) aur \(ib + ib = 2ib\).
Dhyan dein: Yahan sab se zyada ghalti yeh hoti hai ke students \(-(a - ib)\) ko \(-a - ib\) likh dete hain aur jawab zero aa jata hai. Bracket kholte waqt dono terms ka sign badlein.

Step 3: \(2i\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{z - \overline{z}}{2i} = \dfrac{2ib}{2i} = b\]
\[= \operatorname{Im}(z)\]
Kyun: Upar aur neeche dono mein \(2i\) common hai, cancel ho gaya, aur sirf \(b\) bacha, jo imaginary part hai.

Aam ghalti (Common mistake)
\(\operatorname{Im}(z)\) barabar \(b\) hai, \(ib\) nahin. Imaginary part khud aik real number hota hai; \(i\) sirf yeh batata hai ke yeh number kis direction (vertical axis) mein hai. Isi liye formula mein \(2i\) se divide karte hain, sirf 2 se nahin.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal \(z = 3 + 4i\): \(z - \overline{z} = (3 + 4i) - (3 - 4i) = 8i\), aur \(8i/(2i) = 4\). \(3 + 4i\) ka imaginary part waqai 4 hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\dfrac{z - \overline{z}}{2i} = \operatorname{Im}(z)\) (farq lene se real part cancel ho kar sirf imaginary part bachta hai).

blocks.explanation: Proof ka sawal. Pehle samajhte hain \(|z|\) kya hai: yeh modulus hai, yani Argand diagram par origin se point \(z\) tak ka faasla (distance), jaise naqshe par ghar se school ki seedhi doori. Formula: \(|a + ib| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) (Pythagoras theorem se). Yahan dono sides alag alag cheezein lagti hain, aik mein square hai aur doosri mein multiplication. Plan: dono sides ko alag alag simplify karenge aur dikhayenge ke dono \(a^2 + b^2\) ke barabar hain.
steps:
Step 1: \(z = a + ib\) farz karein
\[z = a + ib\]
\[\overline{z} = a - ib\]
Kyun: General shakal, taake proof har complex number ke liye ho.

Step 2: Left side
\[|z| = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\]
\[|z|^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\]
Kyun: Modulus ki definition lagayi, phir square kiya. Square root ka square karne se root khatam ho jata hai, jaise \((\sqrt{9})^2 = 9\).

Step 3: Right side
\[z \cdot \overline{z} = (a + ib)(a - ib)\]
\[= a^{2} - (ib)^{2}\]
\[= a^{2} - i^{2}b^{2}\]
\[= a^{2} + b^{2}\]
Kyun: Yeh shakal \((x + y)(x - y)\) wali hai, jis ka jawab \(x^2 - y^2\) hota hai; yahan \(x = a\) aur \(y = ib\). Phir \((ib)^2 = i^2 b^2\), aur \(i^2 = -1\) ki wajah se \(-i^2 b^2\) ban gaya \(+b^2\).
Dhyan dein: \((ib)^2\) ko \(ib^2\) mat likhein; square \(i\) aur \(b\) dono par lagta hai.

Step 4: Muqabla karein
\[|z|^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} = z \cdot \overline{z}\]
Kyun: Dono sides ka jawab aik hi expression \(a^2 + b^2\) aaya, is liye dono barabar hain. Is ka matlab: kisi complex number ko us ke conjugate se multiply karein to hamesha aik positive real number milta hai.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal \(z = 3 + 4i\): \(|z| = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\), to \(|z|^2 = 25\); aur \((3 + 4i)(3 - 4i) = 9 + 16 = 25\). Dono barabar hain.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(|z|^{2} = z \cdot \overline{z}\) (number ko conjugate se zarb dene se us ke faasle ka square milta hai, jo hamesha real hai).

blocks.explanation: Proof ka sawal, aur yeh part (iii) par khara hai. Pehle aik shart: \(z \ne 0\), kyun ke zero se divide nahin hota. Yahan humein \(1/z\) ko aisi shakal mein likhna hai jis ke neeche koi \(i\) na ho. Sawal yeh hai ke kis cheez se multiply karein? Jawab: conjugate \(\overline{z}\) se, kyun ke part (iii) ne dikhaya ke \(z\overline{z}\) real number \(|z|^2\) hai. Plan: \(1/z\) ke upar neeche \(\overline{z}\) se multiply karein, phir part (iii) ka result laga dein.
steps:
Step 1: Upar neeche \(\overline{z}\) se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1}{z} \cdot \dfrac{\overline{z}}{\overline{z}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\overline{z}}{z\overline{z}}\]
Kyun: \(\overline{z}/\overline{z} = 1\) hai, aur kisi cheez ko 1 se multiply karne se value nahin badalti; sirf shakal badalti hai. \(\overline{z}\) is liye chuna kyun ke \(z\overline{z}\) real number ban jata hai, aur hum yahi chahte hain.

Step 2: Part (iii) use karein
\[z\overline{z} = |z|^{2}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{\overline{z}}{|z|^{2}}\]
Kyun: Part (iii) hum pehle hi saabit kar chuke hain, is liye usay seedha use kar sakte hain. Proofs mein pichle saabit shuda results ka istemal bilkul jaiz hai.

Teaching note
Isi wajah se complex number se divide karte waqt hum hamesha denominator ke conjugate se multiply karte hain: \(\dfrac{1}{a + ib} = \dfrac{a - ib}{a^2 + b^2}\). Yeh formula Sawal 4 (multiplicative inverse) aur Sawal 5 (division) dono ki bunyaad hai, is liye isay achhi tarah yaad kar lein.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal \(z = 3 + 4i\): formula se \(1/z = (3 - 4i)/25\). Ab \((3 + 4i) \cdot \dfrac{3 - 4i}{25} = \dfrac{25}{25} = 1\). \(z\) se multiply karke 1 aaya, yani yeh waqai \(1/z\) hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{\overline{z}}{|z|^{2}}\) (jab \(z \ne 0\)); yani reciprocal nikaalne ke liye conjugate ko modulus ke square se divide karein.
